interpretation.standalone: Five normal and five JIT-disabled processes pass. The host uses a minimum four-millisecond timer shim; it is not equivalent to browser scheduling.
interpretation.staticBrowser: Same compiled bytes fail once in ten normal and once in ten JIT-disabled WebKit attempts. All 20 host attachments record only / and /probe.js with the expected module hash. Vite client, Rust, Wasm, editor DOM and JIT are not necessary for the reduced unexpected-zero symptom.
interpretation.staged: Seven passes, three failures with JIT disabled. At iterations 2471, 9551 and 6871, staged locals all read 2048; temporary values[1] or values[4] plus consumed local read positive zero. Sources also remain correct. Narrowed to array construction/storage/readback or intervening representation conversion, not solely the conditional expression. These remain cold-path observations, not native input/output register snapshots.

nativeCandidate.reason: The numeric-array initializer converts tagged integer/double values using the same instruction pattern implicated in an earlier separate Object.is capture. No causal link or defect at this location is established.

limitations: No established link between this unexpected-zero symptom and every editor fault or the earlier native FCSEL observation.
Passing bounded standalone runs do not prove the browser host causes the fault.
Compiler output differs from Vite output; only the original static and standalone runs here use exact same module bytes.
Failed compiler/setup attempts launched no diagnostic children and are not counted as probe runs.
No installed engine patch, browser preference change, validation relaxation or runtime fix.
